A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Scene-VLM work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary sections are readable and matchable despite repagination and appendix reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-segmentation and video-chaptering results, component ablations, attention analyses, explanation evaluations, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds MovieNet baseline evaluations and comparative computational measurements.

M1.justification: The multimodal shot representation, context–focus windows, sequential Yes/No generation, confidence formula, training objective, and explanation alignment are unchanged. The new Chapter-LLaMA adaptation concerns a comparator, not Scene-VLM.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate cinematic segmentation on MovieNet-318, documentary segmentation on BBC Planet Earth, video chaptering on the same VidChapters-7M subset, and movie-boundary explanations. The added comparisons use existing MovieNet coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the comparison methods: Chapter-LLaMA joins the MovieNet comparison in Table 2, untuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Claude 4.5 Sonnet appear in new Table 11, and TranS4mer joins the computational comparison in Table 12. Chapter-LLaMA previously appeared only in chaptering experiments, and TranS4mer lacked comparative resource measurements.

E3.justification: The added zero-shot comparison uses one frame per shot for all models, LLM parsing for zero-shot outputs, rule-based parsing for Scene-VLM, and negative labels for unparsed shots. The added Chapter-LLaMA experiment supplies per-shot captions, while the computational comparison specifies three frames per shot for TranS4mer. Existing splits, training settings, and evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 tests the necessity of fine-tuning and examines prediction-format failures. B.4 extends the existing computational analysis with an external efficiency comparator. Earlier modality, window, frame-count, model-size, confidence-scheme, threshold, attention, and explanation analyses are retained; the qualitative explanation subsection moves from B.3 to B.5.

E5.justification: Both versions report computational latency means and standard deviations over five runs and maximum memory over those runs. Both retain five-run repeated sampling for the concise prediction scheme. Adding TranS4mer under the existing reporting practice does not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds targeted comparison results: Chapter-LLaMA obtains 38.6 F1/41.5 AP on MovieNet; zero-shot Qwen and Claude obtain 11.1 and 37.6 F1, with parsing-error rates of 7.9% and 0.03%; and TranS4mer uses 1 GB with 0.24 ± 0.0 seconds latency. Existing scores remain unchanged, including Scene-VLM's 62.1 F1/66.8 AP and its one-frame variant's 61.8 F1/65.3 AP.

T1.justification: The shot/context definitions, model-output formulation, softmax and confidence equations, and attention aggregation mathematics are unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: a fine-tuned VLM for scene segmentation, sequential context–focus prediction, confidence extraction, explanation alignment, and benchmark performance. The headline MovieNet improvement claims remain +6 AP and +13.7 F1.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies restricted generative flexibility as a limitation of structured Yes/No outputs. Appendix B.3 interprets the new results as supporting fine-tuning and discusses parsing and confidence-extraction failures. B.4 adds an accuracy-versus-efficiency discussion acknowledging TranS4mer's lower memory and latency.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.2.4 identifies MiniCPM-V as the per-shot captioner for the Chapter-LLaMA adaptation and describes preserving its input format. B.3 documents frame restrictions, parsing methods, and handling of unparsed outputs. Existing frame resolution, LoRA settings, hardware, training duration, and inference details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Claude Sonnet 4.5 and MiniCPM-V and extends empirical positioning against general-purpose VLMs and caption-based chaptering. The related-work overview and central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized wording corrections and clarifications, adds appendix subsections for Chapter-LLaMA adaptation and zero-shot baselines, and moves the supplementary explanation discussion after computational analysis. Most prose and the main section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 11, expands Table 2, and reformats the former computational Table 11 as Table 12 with a parameter-count column and reordered rows. Figures 1 and 6 are reduced in size, and several displays move within the layout. Existing diagrams, plots, and qualitative examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through direct VLM controls and the MovieNet Chapter-LLaMA comparison, while the TranS4mer resource comparison and explicit output-format limitation improve transparency about tradeoffs. These are useful, bounded gains over v1. Some new comparison details remain unspecified, including the LLM parser and how Chapter-LLaMA's AP scores are obtained, limiting the strength and reproducibility of the added evidence.
